definition: InhabitedConcreteAt m concrete w is ∃ b, concrete b ∧ m.ExistsAt w b over the Kant/#487 Ontic signature: some member of the constant candidate domain satisfies the supplied concreteness predicate and exists at w. concrete : E → Prop is a parameter and not world-indexed (as on the #487 branch); no causal, spatiotemporal, material or independence criterion is built in. Its intended instantiation is the adopted sense of #1103, having esse in re (DEF-CONCRETE-ESSE-IN-RE), under which failing it is being abstract; for another supplied predicate it need not be. Concrete is not material: an idealist may count an actual experience as concrete. The world w is an element of the frame; reading it as a complete history rather than a time, and w₀ as the actual world, is the intended interpretation, not part of the Lean type. Inhabitation of the world type or membership in the candidate domain is not population.
note: Stipulated for #536 so that the Cogito result has the exact shape of #487's PopulatedConcreteAt (branch codex/487-necessary-concrete-root, not merged). When #487 lands, one of the two should be defined from the other. The criterion question (#544) is settled for intended interpretations by the owner's adopted esse sense (#1103, 2026-11-06); the Lean parameter stays generic, so every result over it holds for any instantiation.
